Firms often rebrand to counter negative shocks, but can it work? Changing flood insurance demand shifts climate risk across homeowners, lenders, and governments. We show that flood insurance take-up follows rising and falling home equity over the housing boom and bust across markets with different price dynamics. item.description:
Li, Y., Wang, Z., Zhou, S.
As the spread of waste imposes substantial environmental and economic burdens, a newer operational strategy, waste valorization, is gaining attention. Temperature control in refrigerated delivery vehicles is critical for preserving product quality, yet existing approaches neglect critical operational uncertainties, such as stochastic door-opening durations and heterogeneous initial product temperatures. Earlier work by Blanco et al. (2020) found that payback periods appeared stable over time between 2010-2016. item.description:

Fiscal pressure forces public healthcare systems to reduce waiting times via hospital competition, yet patients' bounded rationality weakens this policy. Digital platforms are changing how firms design, coordinate, and govern operations by integrating artificial intelligence, blockchain, digital sensing and digital twins, data infrastructure, and additive manufacturing. Service systems in which demand, congestion, and worker incentives evolve jointly are ubiquitous in modern operations. We study a dynamic principal–agent problem in a queueing system with customer abandonment, where the principal controls arrivals through pricing and the agent privately chooses a costly service rate.
